ky_secret_garden.blurb:
Secret Garden is a sunny sandstone wall in the Miller Fork preserve of the Red River Gorge, with a good spread of sport lines and a smaller share of trad. The rock is mostly vertical, and the bulk of the climbing sits in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a few easier lines at the low end and a handful of 5.12s at the top. Little Wing and Sloppy Seconds are among the favorites here.

The wall faces mostly south and catches sun through most of the day, though one stretch of it goes shady late in the afternoon. It is a short walk from the lot, so expect company on nice weekends.
ky_secret_garden.parking_note: Use the big gravel lot with the kiosk at the end of Hell Creek Road, which you reach from Shoemaker Ridge Road off KY 11. The last miles are rough and slow, so a high-clearance vehicle is a help.
ky_secret_garden.approach: Follow the trail that climbs the hillside behind the big black oil tanks near the lot; it meets the cliff below Linear Regression.

ky_monastery.blurb:
Monastery is a varied sandstone crag in the Miller Fork preserve, mixing sport and trad on terrain that runs from slabby to seriously overhanging. The left end is a steep wall of hard sport lines, the middle holds more moderate slab and vertical climbing, and the right end steepens again with more difficult bolted routes. The Heretic is a rare easier trad line here.

Most of the climbing falls between 5.10 and 5.12, so this is a wall for climbers who already lead solid sport grades, though a few lower-grade options exist in the center. The Suffering and Barking Dogmas are popular picks.
ky_monastery.parking_note: Use the big gravel lot with the kiosk at the end of Hell Creek Road, which you reach from Shoemaker Ridge Road off KY 11. The last miles are rough and slow, so a high-clearance vehicle is a help.
ky_monastery.approach: Cross the footbridge near the lot and bear right on the main trail. After roughly 250 yards a trail breaks sharply right and uphill to the wall; a short connector reaches the middle section, and the main trail continues to the right end.

ky_fruit_wall.blurb:
Fruit Wall is one of the best-regarded walls in the Miller Fork preserve, a sandstone face with a mix of sport and some trad, with fruit-themed route names. Steep, technical, powerful climbing is the draw, and the 5.11 and 5.12 grades are the heart of it, with a lower tier of 5.10 and easier lines. Juju Fruit and Slice of Spice give a taste at the more approachable end.

The wall picks up morning sun and goes shady later in the day, which suits warm weather. The trail arrives near the base of Hourglass Crack, and poison ivy can crowd the trail and the left-hand routes.
ky_fruit_wall.parking_note: Use the big gravel lot with the kiosk at the end of Hell Creek Road, which you reach from Shoemaker Ridge Road off KY 11. The last miles are rough and slow, so a high-clearance vehicle is a help.
ky_fruit_wall.approach: From the lot, cross the footbridge and follow the main road, keeping right at the signed fork and crossing the stream a second time. Where the road climbs and narrows, take the trail on the left up to the base of the wall.

ky_bob_marley.blurb:
Bob Marley is a tall sport amphitheater in the Pendergrass-Murray preserve of the Red River Gorge, and one of the places in the Gorge where harder climbers come to project. Most of the lines sit at 5.12 and up, with a smaller group of 5.11s and a few easier routes. Toker is a typical 5.11a warm-up, while No Redemption and Ultra-perm are well-known lines at the top of the grade range.

The wall is long and tall, so many routes ask for stamina as much as power. It shares a parking area and a connecting cliff-base trail with the neighboring Drive-By crag, so it is easy to combine visits.
ky_bob_marley.parking_note: Drive down Bald Rock Fork Road, which turns to gravel and drops steeply, to the signed lot on the left that serves Bob Marley, Drive-By and Chica Bonita. It is roughly 0.6 miles beyond the Motherlode lot.
ky_bob_marley.approach: Go back to the road, cross it, and follow the gravel track uphill for about 0.2 miles, then take the trail that cuts left up to the wall.

ky_chica_bonita_wall.blurb:
Chica Bonita Wall is a moderate-friendly sandstone face in the Pendergrass-Murray preserve, mixing sport and trad. Unlike many walls nearby, the routes here are mostly vertical rather than steep, which makes it a welcome change for climbers who want technical movement over pump. The grades span the 5.8 to 5.12 range, with the 5.10s and 5.11s making up the largest share.

Brown Eyed Girl and Cheaper Than a Movie are good places to start. The rock is solid, though lines that see little traffic can be a bit dirty, and enough overhang keeps much of the wall dry through a heavy shower.
ky_chica_bonita_wall.parking_note: Drive down Bald Rock Fork Road to the signed lot shared by Drive-By, Bob Marley and Chica Bonita; a 4WD or high-clearance vehicle makes the descent easier.

ky_crossroads_the.blurb:
The Crossroads is a mostly sport sandstone wall in Coal Bank Hollow, in the Pendergrass-Murray preserve, with a small number of easy trad lines mixed in. The climbing is on slabby, crimpy rock, and the grades run widely from the 5.6 range up to 5.13, with the 5.12s the biggest group and a solid supply of 5.10 and 5.11 below that.

The wall generally faces south, though big trees throw plenty of shade in summer, which helps on warm days. Boilerplate and Banjolero are good lines to get a feel for the style.

ky_gold_coast.blurb:
Gold Coast is the far end of the cliff in Coal Bank Hollow, in the Pendergrass-Murray preserve, and it holds both sport and trad on sandstone. The main wall is hard sport climbing in the 5.12 to 5.14 range, with long lines that get taller as you move right. The far right side is mostly traditional, with some very easy lines at the bottom of the grade range.

Expect big, steady-length routes, and note that the tops of the lines can stay wet after rain.

ky_indian_creek.blurb:
Indian Creek in the northern Red River Gorge is a trad crag built around cracks, and it borrows its name from the famous Utah desert area. Nearly everything here is protected with gear, with a few boulder problems added, and the grades cluster from 5.8 to 5.10, with a few hard 5.11 and 5.12 lines on top. Crack Attack and Curiosity are good places to start.

The standout features are huge offwidth roofs, up to around 20 feet. Different buttresses face different ways, which changes both the conditions and the quality of the rock, and the cracks are slow to dry after rain. The long walk in discourages crowds.
ky_indian_creek.parking_note: The lot sits near the river crossing, reached by a long drive on forest roads from KY 77 through the Nada Tunnel.

ky_fortress_wall.blurb:
Fortress Wall is a classic trad cliff in the northern Red River Gorge, popular with climbers learning to place gear because so many of its lines are moderate. The grades run from the 5.4 range through 5.11, with the greatest number between 5.8 and 5.10, and several of the easier routes are two pitches long. Bedtime for Bonzo and Party Time are the friendly ones.

Because it is so approachable, the wall can get crowded and large groups sometimes take over sections. It also gets plenty of sun, which makes it hot in summer.

ky_beer_trailer_crag.blurb:
Beer Trailer Crag is a short-walk sport crag in the Natural Bridge region of the Red River Gorge, known for steep, powerful, bouldery climbing. Most of the routes fall in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, with a few 5.11s, so it suits climbers ready to project hard sport lines. Afternoon Buzz and Cognitive Dissonance are low-5.12 standouts, while Darkness Falls and Falls City are the intimidating steep ones.

A brief uphill trail splits to a left and a right branch, serving different parts of the crag. Gravel parking stands where a roadside store once did.
ky_beer_trailer_crag.parking_note: Park in the gravel lot on the site of the old roadside store; the walls are a very short hike uphill from it.
